Speed Benchmark

1.2.0

VBoy Color GX is a Wii port of VBoy Color, a Virtual Boy emulator that adds color. This page times every kind of scene in the 24 official Virtual Boy games and two unreleased ones. A scene is at full speed when every 50-frame stretch stays under 19.9 ms a frame.

This is a work in progress, and there’s no public Wii U release yet. Switch between the current release, 1.2.0, timed in Dolphin and on a real Wii and vWii, and the version in development, where the speed work shows up as it happens. Each development build takes the next patch number, 1.2.1-dev, 1.2.2-dev and so on, on the way to 1.3.0. The Wii U version gets timed once every game runs at full speed on the Wii and vWii.

    How it’s measured

    Each scene is a save state and a script of real play, the busiest normal play of that scene. On every machine, a bench build of VBoy Color GX plays the scenes and times how long it takes to emulate each 50-frame stretch, skipping the first stretch while the state loads.

    Dolphin counts emulated time, so its times estimate a real Wii, which can be a little slower in busy scenes.

    This benchmark’s automation was made with AI assistance. For each game, one AI agent records and plays the scenes, and a second agent checks that every replay is exact and looks for busier play. Scripts then time each scene in Dolphin and on the consoles, and add the results to this page. On a real Wii, vWii or Wii U, the script sends the bench over the network with wiiload, and the console sends its times back the same way.
